prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Dispatch Center (Juniper) continuously intakes, triages, dispatches, coordinates under approved protocols; jurisdictions retain resource ownership/local policy. Juniper creates incident records, preserves reports/clarifications, tracks coverage and escalates gaps. Call Taker Mara (Larkspur) confirms/repeats location before medical details, distinguishes observed/reported facts, updates records before dispatch, produces Caller Location Correction Slip, confirms incident ID/receiving facility before destination requests, receives Bedside Arrival Receipt, and verifies arrival time against dispatch timeline/crew communications. Computer Aided Dispatch Console presents incident, priority, maps, travel, availability, constraints, staging, and surge level; verify currency. Triage Supervisor (Copperfield) reviews uncertain, conflicting, deteriorating, severe/escalation cases; assigns/document priorities by immediacy, time sensitivity, deterioration risk; urgent threats receive highest available priority and prompt dispatch. Sends Pediatric Acuity Note; advises demand-related repositioning; refers unusual cases to Regional Medical Director when time permits. Regional Medical Director sets policy, advises clinical needs, elevated-demand priorities, specialized/protocol destinations; no dispatch authority. Data Quality Officer (Pebble) flags defects, audits completeness/compliance/rationales, sends Duplicate Incident Audit Memo, routes corrections operationally, reviews incomplete arrival/handover fields; cannot change priority. Ambulance Coordination Platform consolidates suitable units, time-stamps status/movement, presents approved destination/instructions; selection weighs priority, clinical need, travel, capability/readiness, constraints, coverage. Juniper verifies battery readiness via swap voucher, congestion via queue snapshot; North Gate Status Board displays queue/access restrictions; South Gate Status Board displays south-entrance access and produces South Access Lane Notice for material constraints. Dispatchers compare response times with remaining coverage before moves. Shift Commander (Sundial) approves coverage-reducing/nonstandard exceptions, reviews staging/access and surge coverage, sends Mutual Aid Release Form; escalates unresolved destination/access issues. Hospital Liaison Desk obtains capacity, coordinates destination consultation, records outcomes/restrictions, uses Pediatric Acuity Note with receiving staff, resolves handover questions; Emergency Department reports capacity/access/receiving changes and clarifies patient identity/transfer-document discrepancies with Paramedic Crew before crew clears. Radio Coordinator (Mistral) confirms talkgroup/reachability, transmits ID/location/priority/assignment/hazards and destination instructions over Regional Radio Network; retries unacknowledged messages, alerts supervisor. Network supports en-route updates. Ambulance Unit 417 reports

New part:
S181: Call Taker Mara obtains the age, weight when available, and caregiver observations needed to support pediatric triage.
S182: Paramedic Crew reassesses pediatric patients during transport and reports material changes to the receiving facility.
S183: Kestrel shall confirm that facility capacity and pediatric service limitations are communicated to dispatch before a destination is finalized.
S184: Riverside Trauma Center advises Hospital Liaison Desk when trauma intake conditions may affect the suitability of an otherwise appropriate destination.
S185: Emergency Department staff acknowledge destination changes through the established coordination channel and identify any immediate access restrictions.
S186: Hospital Liaison Desk records facility responses in the regional coordination record and keeps dispatch informed of unresolved constraints.
S187: Mutual aid is requested when local staffed units cannot meet the declared response objectives or when a specialized resource is unavailable.
S188: Regional Radio Network carries mutual-aid requests, acceptance confirmations, and operational updates using the agreed regional call signs.
S189: Copperfield shall approve any temporary triage override and document its rationale before the override is applied.
S190: Ambulance Coordination Platform tracks accepted mutual-aid assignments separately from locally staffed resources to preserve an accurate coverage view.
S191: Ambulance Unit 417 may be reassigned only after dispatch confirms that its current patient-care and transport obligations permit the change.
S192: Fleet Maintenance Cell reports a vehicle restriction promptly so dispatch does not count an unavailable unit toward operational coverage.
S193: Triage Supervisor reviews the audit memo before closing a suspected duplicate incident.
S194: Data Quality Officer reviews unresolved record discrepancies through the established quality process without delaying active patient care.
S195: North Gate Status Board provides a current view of access conditions that may affect ambulance approach or handover timing.
S196: South Gate Status Board provides the equivalent access view for routes and entry points on the southern side of the region.
S197: After surge conditions ease, Shift Commander confirms that outstanding assignments, destination constraints, and staffing gaps have been handed over to the next operational period.
S198: Regional Dispatch Center maintains a degraded-radio procedure that prioritizes emergency traffic and preserves a common operating picture.
S199: Regional Radio Network operators announce channel outages, affected areas, and expected restoration times over the remaining service channels.
S200: Radio Coordinator directs crews to approved fallback channels when the primary channel is unusable.
S201: Crews acknowledge each fallback assignment and repeat critical location and destination details before moving.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
